mouse-unforced-visual-contrast-wheel.description: Head-fixed mice view one or two Gabor patches on lateral screens and use a wheel to report the side with visual evidence, while trials with no visible stimulus can be rewarded for withholding movement. choice.action_mapping: Licking the spout within the response window after a stimulus change is a go response (hit). Withholding licking through the response window is a no-go response (miss on change trials, correct rejection on catch trials). Licking before the change window is an aborted trial.

mouse-visual-change-detection-allen.description: Head-fixed mice view a stream of natural images flashed at a fixed cadence (250 ms image, 500 ms gray) and must lick within a short response window after the image identity changes. A subset of trials are catch trials in which the image does not change, and the mouse must withhold licking. The task is the standardized behavioral protocol used by the Allen Institute Visual Behavior 2P and Visual Behavior Neuropixels datasets.
expected_analyses: hit rate, miss rate, false-alarm rate, correct-rejection rate

feedback.penalty: No active punishment beyond reward omission and trial abort on early licks.

interpretive_claims.caveat: The change-detection paradigm probes detection of a categorical transition. Reading it as a measure of generic perceptual sensitivity conflates change detection with novelty, image-set learning, and task-rule familiarity.
interpretive_claims.label: visual change detection

stimulus.evidence_schedule: A repeating sequence of identical natural-image flashes is shown until a pseudo-randomly scheduled change time, at which point one image is replaced by a different image drawn from the same image set. On catch trials the scheduled change does not occur and the mouse must withhold licking through the response window.
stimulus.notes: The relevant operational evidence is a categorical image transition, not a scalar contrast or coherence value. Image identity, change time, and catch-trial flag are preserved as task variables.

mouse-visual-contrast-lick-gonogo.description: Head-fixed mice view target and non-target visual stimuli, including variable-contrast conditions, and report the target class by licking or withholding a lick.
